correctness.rationale: Every admissible pair lies in one of 1728 faces obtained by choosing one tight signed facet for x, y and x-y. Exact Q(sqrt(3)) elimination shows that 168 of these faces are nonempty and every non-point face is a segment. Along a segment, A=N(x+y) and B=N(2x-y) are nonnegative convex piecewise-affine functions. Therefore (A+B)/2 and (A^2+B^2)/2 are convex and attain their maxima at endpoints. Exact endpoint evaluation gives sqrt(3) and 3. The explicit pair x=(1,sqrt(3)-2), y=(sqrt(3)-1,sqrt(3)-1) has all three required unit norms and A=B=sqrt(3). Concavity of sqrt then gives M3<=sqrt(M1)=3^(1/4), with equality at the same pair.
risks: The proof is computation-assisted for the polyhedral endpoint census, but the enumeration is exact and exhaustive rather than sampled.
The M3 proof depends on the exact M1 bound and an analytic Jensen inequality, not on finite enumeration of the nonlinear objective.

value.rationale: These constants were introduced to quantify midline geometry of Minkowski equilateral triangles, and the source explicitly leaves further geometric characterization as an open direction. The regular dodecagon is a canonical symmetric non-Hilbert polyhedral plane. Showing that all three constants simultaneously equal their Hilbert values demonstrates a concrete limitation of the combined invariants as Hilbert detectors, not merely an isolated numerical table entry. The exact facet-endpoint method also gives a reusable route for computing M1 and M2 on other polygonal norms.
risks: The finding is a canonical counterintuitive benchmark rather than a classification of all spaces with Hilbert-value collisions.
